scope: Source-specific review. Source fields/products and fetched selected bytes are immutable; explicit domain/assay scope does not establish all natural-product activity.

decision_summaries.reason: The original study directly tested recombinant human NC4 with rat COMP, whose P35444 accession is explicitly named in Methods, including full COMP and its 266–755 fragment. COMP is an extracellular matrix constituent, so refine the positive interaction to extracellular matrix binding. Preserve the mixed-species partner and heparin-competition scope; this is not a new adaptor mechanism or evidence for equal activity of every natural COL9A1 product. The refinement is semantic ligand specificity, not a claimed current is_a edge from protein binding.

Retain the positive association with the exact 236-residue GIPC1 isoform O14908-2, reconstructed from its recorded N-terminal deletion and matched to all three array, pooling and validated two-hybrid records. The canonical PDZ-containing identity and possible G-protein-linked context do not resolve a more specific binding activity for this pair. Yeast assay positivity is retained without a native cellular pathway, PDZ-interface or isoform-specific signaling claim.

Three positive two-hybrid records match canonical 173-residue CRYAA. Its official experimental functional annotation establishes a protein chaperone that prevents aggregation; GO:0051087 names binding to that partner class. Refine the accepted interaction without asserting that COL9A1 itself folds proteins or that this screen measured a folding reaction. The human products were tested in yeast, and natural colocalization or a specific contact interface was not established.

Three positive two-hybrid records match the 244-residue KLK6 precursor. Official identity and direct activity annotations establish its serine-protease class, fitting protease binding more specifically than enzyme binding. Preserve the precursor and assay scope: processing, active-enzyme state, substrate cleavage and the contacted region were not measured in these records. The caspase and ubiquitin-specific-protease children do not describe KLK6.

The positive association has a verified collagen counterpart, canonical human COL6A1/P12109. Two exact anti-tag affinity-purification records occur in HEK293T and HCT116 contexts; one is a spoke-expanded complex association. Collagen binding narrows the partner class while preserving AP-MS/co-complex evidence. It does not claim isolated binary affinity, native cartilage contact or a specific multichain topology.

The secretion event includes both luminal precursor input and extracellular collagen output; this assertion concerns the destination. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The event specifically places collagen IX at the surface of type II fibrils through covalent cross-links, consistent with the human cartilage source. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The event contains extracellular collagen IX within the integrin alpha1beta1/alpha2beta1 ligand set; participant membership is not an isolated alpha1-chain affinity assay for every integrin. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The NCAM1 event includes collagen IX as an extracellular ligand context, without assigning neural adhesion machinery activity to the alpha1 chain. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The PDGF event places collagen-containing matrix among growth-factor retention partners; this does not make COL9A1 a PDGF receptor or establish an isolated chain-specific binding constant. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The alpha10beta1 integrin event includes extracellular collagen IX material, with the chain represented through its complex. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The alpha11beta1 event explicitly concerns extracellular collagen IX ligand material; the complex-level ligand description is not an all-isoform assay. The actual event summary and typed participant path to P20849 were inspected. Retain this source-specific extracellular location; underlying event citations were not all independently recovered.

The canonical alpha1(IX)/alpha2(IX)/alpha3(IX) heterotrimer fits the exact current type IX definition and direct target assembly evidence. The target appearing as its own PAINT descendant source is expected, not circular. Current same-term target records corroborate the placement; the historical ancestral node/tree was not reconstructed.

Original human cartilage analysis identifies type IX chains and maps native type II–IX and IX–IX cross-links. Retain alpha1(IX) membership in the defined heterotrimer, separating those native network observations from recombinant constructs and from an alpha1–alpha1 homodimer claim.

The actual structure assembles alpha1/alpha2/alpha3 IX NC2 chains attached to engineered type I collagen host–guest triple-helical sequences. It establishes a target-chain trimerization/stagger interface consistent with type IX membership. It is not a structure of intact collagen IX or proof that the truncated natural product retains assembly competence.

Retain established type IX heterotrimer membership with curator deference and independent assembly evidence. The complete authentic cited abstract establishes human COL9A1/COL9A2 gene and alternative-exon structure; its full text was not recovered, so it is not described as a newly read purified assembly experiment.

The signal-bearing precursor enters the ER lumen for chain assembly before secretion. Current ARBA00028691 still emits this term, and its IPR008160/IPR013320/Primates branch matches the current official target record. This corroborates a biosynthetic compartment rather than a mature-matrix core location or a chaperone/catalytic activity.

The triple-helix formation event places collagen precursors in the ER lumen while other proteins perform hydroxylation/isomerization and chaperone functions. Retain the precursor location outside the principal extracellular core; actual event membership was traced without importing other participants' catalytic functions.

The secretion event has an ER-luminal precursor input, distinct from its extracellular output reviewed separately. Retain the precursor location outside the principal extracellular core; actual event membership was traced without importing other participants' catalytic functions.

The type IX chain-association event places the precursor complex in the ER lumen. Its general C-terminal-propeptide narrative must not obscure direct IX evidence for NC2 and additional domain contributions. Retain the precursor location outside the principal extracellular core; actual event membership was traced without importing other participants' catalytic functions.

Current ARBA00028067 emits animal organ morphogenesis and its exact FunFam 2.60.120.200:FF:000105 branch 83 matches the official target record. The present rule premise is real. Its biological specificity remains unresolved: the bounded evidence does not identify a performed organ-morphogenesis contribution, while extracellular structural work could in principle contribute. The narrower 1987 TAS citation is assessed separately; neither that paper nor the current match reconstructs the historical rule training/assignment.

The complete original five-page article studies chicken embryonic cartilage cDNA/genomic sequences and purified collagen fragments, including genuine alpha1/alpha2 NC3 comparisons. It explains molecular structure and the glycosaminoglycan attachment sequence, but does not establish a step in generating or organizing an animal organ. This source-specific process attribution is over-extended; the judgment does not deny COL9A1 structural contributions to development and is not a wrong-gene conclusion from the alpha2-focused abstract.

decision_summaries.reason: Native human alpha1(IX)-containing collagen IX participates in covalent links with the type II/IX matrix. The collagen convention supports the structural inference from type IX membership. This is fibril-associated matrix contribution, not an isolated tensile-force measurement or autonomous fibrillar-collagen assembly.

decision_summaries.reason: Retain the structural collagen interpretation while distinguishing it from what the source measured. Actual human ECM-enrichment/MS Methods and original supplementary row121 identify a grouped COL9A1 entry labeled Isoform Short. The RCA classification and established collagen biology support the structural term; mass-spectrometric detection itself does not measure tensile mechanics or isolate a natural product's activity.

Alpha1(IX) contributes physical chain interfaces and matrix cross-links that organize the extracellular matrix, fitting the existing process definition. Direct human cartilage and engineered assembly evidence corroborate the inherited matrix role. Current donor identities and same-term records were traced without reconstructing the historical PAINT tree or treating a small source set as weak evidence.

Original human NC4 surface-plasmon-resonance and solid-phase assays directly measure heparin binding. Replace the generic carbohydrate term with heparin binding at the observed ligand scope. This is a semantic refinement, not an assertion that the current typed ontology places heparin binding under carbohydrate binding; equivalence among natural splice products is not inferred.

Full original Methods were not recovered, so exact construct boundaries and further controls are not claimed. Replace the generic carbohydrate term with heparin binding at the observed ligand scope. Actual ECM-enriched human normal/tumor colon and liver samples contain a grouped COL9A1 protein entry in original supplementary row121 of both complete and matrisome sheets. Its principal accession is P20849-2, with other COL9A1 products in the group. Retain extracellular matrix location, without claiming isoform-exclusive peptides, disease-specific causality or every sample being positive.

The extracellular matrix location is independently supported by native human cartilage chain/cross-link work and human ECM proteomics. Current donor identities and literal records corroborate the inherited localization. The target is a legitimate source of its own PAINT inference; neither that self-entry nor donor count is a reason to reject the placement.

Retain contextual self-association with the two sources distinguished. The original human cartilage paper maps alpha1(IX) links to type II and alpha3(IX) NC1 rather than independently resolving an alpha1–alpha1 homodimer. Separately, actual PMID:17880280 Results report predominantly monomers and dimers when full-length human alpha1(IX) is expressed individually in insect cells. This supports a non-core recombinant dimer context, not a native homodimer core or equal activity of all natural products. The public source-evidence index, followup_source_clarifications, provides the original postprint Results/Figure 3 locator and a short literal excerpt; the unchanged normal abstract is not the source of this dimer observation.

original_term.label: negative regulation of activation of membrane attack complex

decision_summaries.reason: Recombinant human alpha1(IX) NC4 directly inhibits purified C9 polymerization and reduces cell-associated polymeric C9 with appropriate positive/negative controls and accompanying hemolysis assays. The domain performs inhibitory work at terminal-complement assembly; this is not inferred from precursor necessity or a downstream knockout effect. The pAM104-2 human NC4 construct is authenticated through original PMID:19700767 Methods; exact residue endpoints were not resolved. Restrict the assertion to the tested recombinant domain, not intact collagen IX, every splice product or a demonstrated endogenous immune role. NC4 is not itself a factor-I cofactor or protease, although it enhances reactions containing FH/C4BP. Current typed coverage has no overlap with original or replacement terms; same-role CLU carries direct IDA1971, while VTN/COMP exact-query absences are retained. No redundant parent or complement-binding NEW is proposed.

ontology_definitions.name: extracellular region

definition.text: The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

ontology_definitions.comment: Note that this term is intended to annotate gene products that are not attached to the cell surface. For gene products at the cell surface, consider annotating to external side of plasma membrane ; GO:0009897.

Binding to collagen, a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals. Collagen is highly enriched in glycine (some regions are 33% glycine) and proline, occurring predominantly as 3-hydroxyproline (about 20%).

ontology_definitions.name: extracellular matrix structural constituent conferring tensile strength

definition.text: A constituent of the extracellular matrix that enables the matrix to resist longitudinal stress.

Cyclitols are generally not regarded as carbohydrates.

The binding activity of a molecule that brings together two or more molecules through a selective, non-covalent, often stoichiometric interaction, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way.

Morphogenesis of an animal organ. An organ is defined as a tissue or set of tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Morphogenesis is the process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

current_matrix_definition.name: obsolete collagen-containing extracellular matrix

definition.text: OBSOLETE. An extracellular matrix consisting mainly of proteins (especially collagen) and glycosaminoglycans (mostly as proteoglycans) that provides not only essential physical scaffolding for the cellular constituents but can also initiate crucial biochemical and biomechanical cues required for tissue morphogenesis, differentiation and homeostasis. The components are secreted by cells in the vicinity and form a sheet underlying or overlying cells such as endothelial and epithelial cells.

current_matrix_definition.comment: This term was obsoleted because it was not clearly defined and usage has been inconsistent.

core_functions.description: Alpha1(IX) supplies structural elements of the alpha1/alpha2/alpha3 type IX heterotrimer at the surface of type II collagen fibrils. Chain assembly and covalent matrix connections support this fibril-associated matrix role. The NC2 structure is an engineered assembly-domain assay, and the chain does not autonomously form the major fibrillar scaffold or catalyze its own processing. Long/short precursor architecture and the severely truncated product are kept distinct.

molecular_function.label: extracellular matrix structural constituent conferring tensile strength

core_functions.description: The alpha1(IX) NC4 domain binds heparin, providing a ligand-binding activity in the extracellular matrix distinct from structural chain assembly. Recombinant human NC4 binding is supported by direct assays, GAG competition and a folding-controlled basic-region mutant; full-length recombinant human collagen IX also binds heparin. Additional binding sites on the intact heterotrimer are not all assigned to alpha1. These experiments do not demonstrate a specific native matrix-bridging mechanism or equivalent activity of all natural splice products, including the NC4-lacking Short product.
